capabilities.title: Cache and inspect intermediate activations with run_with_cache
capabilities.summary: Wrap a supported model in HookedTransformer and capture residual-stream, attention, and MLP activations by documented cache key and shape.

when: Intermediate activations (residual stream, attention patterns, MLP outputs) are needed for analysis.
Studying attention patterns or information flow in a GPT-style transformer.
avoid_when: Non-transformer architectures — use nnsight or pyvene.
Training or analyzing Sparse Autoencoders — use SAELens.
Remote execution on massive models — use nnsight with NDIF.
Higher-level causal-intervention abstractions are wanted — use pyvene.

steps: Load a supported model (50+ families: GPT-2, LLaMA, Pythia, Mistral, ...) with HookedTransformer.from_pretrained; gated models (LLaMA, Mistral) need HF_TOKEN set in the environment.
Tokenize with model.to_tokens(prompt).
Run logits, cache = model.run_with_cache(tokens).
Index the cache by documented key and shape: cache['resid_post', L] [batch,pos,d_model]; cache['pattern', L] [batch,head,q_pos,k_pos]; cache['mlp_out', L]; q/k/v per head.
Bound memory on large models with names_filter=lambda n: ... and device='cpu'.

recovery: Memory explosion with large models: cache selectively via names_filter and cache on CPU.

capabilities.title: Activation patching (causal tracing) over layer x position
capabilities.summary: Patch clean-run activations into corrupted runs at each (layer, position) and measure a behavior metric to localize which activations causally drive the output.

when: Identifying which layers/positions causally affect a model behavior.
Running causal-tracing experiments between minimal-pair prompts.

steps: Define clean and corrupted prompts that differ minimally (e.g., 'The Eiffel Tower...' vs 'The Colosseum...').
Cache clean activations with run_with_cache.
Define a metric capturing the behavior difference (e.g., logit difference between the two candidate answer tokens).
For each (layer, position): run model.run_with_hooks on corrupted tokens with a hook that copies the clean activation into blocks.{layer}.hook_resid_post at that position; record the metric.
Visualize the layer x position result matrix as a heatmap and identify causal hotspots.

validation: The metric separates clean vs corrupted baselines before any patching.
recovery: Stale hooks corrupting results: always model.reset_hooks() before re-running.
Unexpected token positions: verify tokenization with model.to_str_tokens and check prepend_bos — multi-token words shift positions.

capabilities.title: Direct logit attribution by attention head (IOI-style circuit analysis)
capabilities.summary: Decompose a prediction into per-head contributions by projecting each head's output through W_O and W_U, then rank heads and confirm with ablation.

when: Decomposing which attention heads drive a specific prediction.
Identifying circuit components (e.g., name movers, S-inhibition, induction heads) for a task like IOI.

steps: Set up the task with clear target tokens (IOI: logit difference between indirect object ' John' and subject ' Mary').
Compute the baseline logit difference from a cached run.
Per (layer, head): contribution = cache['z', layer][0, :, head, :][-1] @ model.W_O[layer, head] @ model.W_U, read off the target-token difference.
Map contributions across all heads and rank the top contributors.
Validate the identified components with ablation experiments.

validation: Ablating the top-attributed heads moves the logit difference in the expected direction.

capabilities.title: Detect induction heads via repeated-token attention
capabilities.summary: Score every head's attention from the repeated token back to its successor on an [A][B]...[A] sequence; high scorers are induction-head candidates.

when: Locating induction heads implementing the [A][B]...[A] -> [B] pattern.
Checking a model's in-context copying machinery.

steps: Build a repeated-token sequence (e.g., tokens [A, B, A]).
Run run_with_cache and read cache['pattern', layer] per layer.
Score attention from the second [A] position back to the [B] position for every head.
Take the top-k scores across (layer, head) as induction-head candidates.

capabilities.title: TransformerLens analysis pitfalls and version constraints
capabilities.summary: The recurring correctness traps — stale hooks, tokenization surprises, skipped LayerNorm, memory blowups — plus supported-model and version facts.

when: Writing or reviewing any TransformerLens analysis code.

steps: Always model.reset_hooks() after run_with_hooks debugging — old hooks persist silently otherwise.
Never assume tokenization: check model.to_str_tokens explicitly ('Neel' -> ['Ne','el']) and mind prepend_bos.
Include LayerNorm when reading pre-activations: use blocks[layer].ln2(residual) before multiplying by W_in, not the raw residual.
Bound memory on large models: names_filter + device='cpu' in run_with_cache.
Model support: 50+ families (GPT-2, LLaMA, Pythia, GPT-J, Mistral, Phi, Qwen, OPT, Gemma).
Version notes: v2.0 removed HookedSAE (moved to SAELens); v3.0-alpha adds TransformerBridge for arbitrary nn.Modules.
